title: Hubble Asteroid Hunter AI Discovers 1,031 Uncatalogued Asteroids in Archival Data
aiSystem: Google Cloud AutoML Object-Detection CNN + Citizen-Science Training
whyItMatters: Deep learning trained on citizen-scientist labels mined 19 years of archival Hubble Space Telescope images to discover 1,031 previously uncatalogued asteroids, probing sub-kilometer main-belt populations.
summary: Pablo García-Martín, Sandor Kruk, Marcel Popescu, Bruno Merín, and collaborators (ESA, Zooniverse, and Google Cloud) combined citizen-science classifications from >11,000 volunteers with a deep object-detection neural network to scan 37,000 archival Hubble Space Telescope images spanning 19 years (2002–2021). Published across Astronomy & Astrophysics (2022–2024, vol. 683 A122), the pipeline uncovered 1,701 curved asteroid trails—including 1,031 previously uncatalogued objects—and used Hubble’s orbital parallax curvature to characterize 454 unknown main-belt asteroids mostly under 1 km in size, extending the known main-belt magnitude distribution two magnitudes fainter.
technicalHighlights: Deep object-detection network trained on Zooniverse citizen-science labels systematically scanned 37,000 archival Hubble ACS/WFC and WFC3/UVIS exposures.
Identified 1,031 previously uncatalogued Solar System object trails (~61% of all detections) invisible to ground-based asteroid surveys.
Orbital parallax fitting characterized 454 newly discovered sub-kilometer main-belt asteroids, extending main-belt size–frequency constraints down to absolute magnitude H ≈ 20.
caveats: Because detections come from single-epoch archival exposures spanning two decades, individual newly found asteroids generally cannot be orbit-recovered for targeted follow-up.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated that deep archival vision turns pointed space-telescope archives into serendipitous small-body Solar System surveys.
scoreRationale.ripple: Provides a template for automated archival asteroid, lens, and transient mining across Euclid, JWST, and Roman archives.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Astronomy & Astrophysics with parallax-derived physical catalogs submitted to the IAU Minor Planet Center.
scoreRationale.velocity: Extracted >1,000 new asteroids from 19 years of existing data at zero additional space-telescope observing cost.
